1023def matilda_plots(output_MATILDA, parameter):
1024    """ MATILDA plotting function to plot input data, runoff output and HBV parameters."""
1025
1026    # resampling the output to the specified frequency
1027    def plot_data(output_MATILDA, parameter):
1028        if "Qobs" in output_MATILDA[0].columns:
1029            obs = output_MATILDA[0]["Qobs"].resample(parameter.freq).agg(pd.DataFrame.sum, skipna=False)
1030        if "Q_DDM" in output_MATILDA[0].columns:
1031            if "Q_DDM_scaled" in output_MATILDA[0].columns:
1032                plot_data = output_MATILDA[0].resample(parameter.freq).agg(
1033                    {"T2": "mean", "RRR": "sum", "PE": "sum", "Q_HBV": "sum", \
1034                    "Q_DDM": "sum", "Q_DDM_scaled": "sum", "Q_Total": "sum", "HBV_AET": "sum", "HBV_snowpack": "mean", \
1035                     "HBV_soil_moisture": "mean", "HBV_upper_gw": "mean", "HBV_lower_gw": "mean"}, skipna=False)
1036            else:
1037                plot_data = output_MATILDA[0].resample(parameter.freq).agg(
1038                    {"T2": "mean", "RRR": "sum", "PE": "sum", "Q_HBV": "sum", \
1039                    "Q_DDM": "sum", "Q_DDM_updated_scaled": "sum", "Q_Total": "sum", "HBV_AET": "sum", "HBV_snowpack": "mean", \
1040                     "HBV_soil_moisture": "mean", "HBV_upper_gw": "mean", "HBV_lower_gw": "mean"}, skipna=False)
1041        else:
1042            plot_data = output_MATILDA[0].resample(parameter.freq).agg(
1043                {"T2": "mean", "RRR": "sum", "PE": "sum", "Q_HBV": "sum", \
1044                  "Q_Total": "sum", "HBV_AET": "sum", "HBV_snowpack": "mean", \
1045                 "HBV_soil_moisture": "mean", "HBV_upper_gw": "mean", "HBV_lower_gw": "mean"}, skipna=False)
1046        if "Qobs" in output_MATILDA[0].columns:
1047            plot_data["Qobs"] = obs
1048        # plot_data.loc[plot_data.isnull().any(axis=1), :] = np.nan
1049
1050
1051        plot_annual_data = output_MATILDA[0].copy()
1052        plot_annual_data["month"] = plot_annual_data.index.month
1053        plot_annual_data["day"] = plot_annual_data.index.day
1054        plot_annual_data = plot_annual_data.groupby(["month", "day"]).mean()
1055        plot_annual_data["date"] = pd.date_range(parameter.sim_start, freq='D', periods=len(plot_annual_data)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
1056        plot_annual_data = plot_annual_data.set_index(plot_annual_data["date"])
1057        plot_annual_data.index = pd.to_datetime(plot_annual_data.index)
1058        plot_annual_data["plot"] = 0
1059        plot_annual_data = plot_annual_data.resample(parameter.freq).sum()
1060
1061        return plot_data, plot_annual_data
1062
1063    # Plotting the meteorological parameters
1064    def plot_meteo(plot_data, parameter):
1065        fig, (ax1, ax2, ax3) = plt.subplots(3, sharex=True, figsize=(10, 6))
1066        ax1.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), (plot_data["T2"]), c="#d7191c")
1067        if parameter.freq == "Y":
1068            ax2.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["RRR"], color="#2c7bb6")
1069        else:
1070            ax2.bar(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["RRR"], width=10, color="#2c7bb6")
1071        ax3.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["PE"], c="#008837")
1072        plt.xlabel("Date", fontsize=9)
1073        ax1.grid(linewidth=0.25), ax2.grid(linewidth=0.25), ax3.grid(linewidth=0.25)
1074        ax3.sharey(ax2)
1075        ax1.set_title("Mean temperature", fontsize=9)
1076        ax2.set_title("Precipitation sum", fontsize=9)
1077        ax3.set_title("Evapotranspiration sum", fontsize=9)
1078        ax1.set_ylabel("[°C]", fontsize=9)
1079        ax2.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9)
1080        ax3.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9)
1081        if str(plot_data.index.values[1])[:4] == str(plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4]:
1082            fig.suptitle(
1083                parameter.freq_long + " meteorological input parameters in " + str(plot_data.index.values[-1])[
1084                                                                               :4],
1085                size=14)
1086        else:
1087            fig.suptitle(
1088                parameter.freq_long + " meteorological input parameters in " + str(plot_data.index.values[0])[
1089                                                                               :4] + "-" + str(
1090                    plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4], size=14)
1091        plt.tight_layout()
1092        fig.set_size_inches(10, 6)
1093        return fig
1094
1095    def plot_runoff(plot_data, plot_annual_data, parameter):
1096        plot_data["plot"] = 0
1097        # plot_data.loc[plot_data.isnull().any(axis=1), :] = np.nan
1098        fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=2, figsize=(14, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [2.75, 1]})
1099        if 'Qobs' in plot_data.columns:
1100            ax1.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["Qobs"], c="#E69F00", label="", linewidth=1.2)
1101        ax1.fill_between(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["plot"], plot_data["Q_HBV"], color='#56B4E9',
1102                         alpha=.75, label="")
1103        if "Q_DDM" in plot_data.columns:
1104            ax1.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["Q_Total"], c="k", label="", linewidth=0.75, alpha=0.75)
1105            ax1.fill_between(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["Q_HBV"], plot_data["Q_Total"], color='#CC79A7',
1106                             alpha=.75, label="")
1107        ax1.set_ylabel("Runoff [mm]", fontsize=9)
1108        if isinstance(output_MATILDA[1], float):
1109            anchored_text = AnchoredText('KGE coeff ' + str(round(output_MATILDA[1], 2)), loc=1, frameon=False)
1110        elif 'Qobs' not in plot_data.columns:
1111            anchored_text = AnchoredText(' ', loc=2, frameon=False)
1112        else:
1113            anchored_text = AnchoredText('KGE coeff exceeds boundaries', loc=2, frameon=False)
1114        ax1.add_artist(anchored_text)
1115        if 'Qobs' in plot_annual_data.columns:
1116            ax2.plot(plot_annual_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_annual_data["Qobs"], c="#E69F00",
1117                     label="Observations", linewidth=1.2)
1118        ax2.fill_between(plot_annual_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_annual_data["plot"], plot_annual_data["Q_HBV"], color='#56B4E9',
1119                         alpha=.75, label="MATILDA catchment runoff")
1120        if "Q_DDM" in plot_annual_data.columns:
1121            ax2.plot(plot_annual_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_annual_data["Q_Total"], c="k", label="MATILDA total runoff",
1122                     linewidth=0.75, alpha=0.75)
1123            ax2.fill_between(plot_annual_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_annual_data["Q_HBV"], plot_annual_data["Q_Total"], color='#CC79A7',
1124                             alpha=.75, label="MATILDA glacial runoff")
1125        ax2.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator(interval=3))
1126        ax2.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%b'))
1127        ax2.set_ylabel("Runoff [mm]", fontsize=9)
1128        if str(plot_data.index.values[1])[:4] == str(plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4]:
1129            plt.suptitle(
1130                parameter.freq_long + " MATILDA simulation for the period " + str(plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4],
1131                size=14)
1132        else:
1133            plt.suptitle(parameter.freq_long + " MATILDA simulation for the period " + str(plot_data.index.values[0])[
1134                                                                                       :4] + "-" + str(
1135                plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4], size=14)
1136        handles, labels = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
1137        fig.legend(handles, labels, loc='lower center', ncol=4, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02),
1138                   bbox_transform=plt.gcf().transFigure)
1139        plt.tight_layout()
1140        fig.subplots_adjust(bottom=0.12)
1141        return fig
1142
1143    # Plotting the HBV output parameters
1144    def plot_hbv(plot_data, parameter):
1145        fig, (ax1, ax2, ax3, ax4, ax5) = plt.subplots(5, sharex=True, figsize=(10, 6))
1146        ax1.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["HBV_AET"], "k")

1149        ax4.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["HBV_upper_gw"], "k")
1150        ax5.plot(plot_data.index.to_pydatetime(), plot_data["HBV_lower_gw"], "k")
1151        ax1.set_title("Actual evapotranspiration", fontsize=9)
1152        ax2.set_title("Soil moisture", fontsize=9)
1153        ax3.set_title("Water in snowpack", fontsize=9)
1154        ax4.set_title("Upper groundwater box", fontsize=9)
1155        ax5.set_title("Lower groundwater box", fontsize=9)
1156        plt.xlabel("Date", fontsize=9)
1157        ax1.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9), ax2.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9), ax3.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9)
1158        ax4.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9), ax5.set_ylabel("[mm]", fontsize=9)
1159        if str(plot_data.index.values[1])[:4] == str(plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4]:
1160            fig.suptitle(parameter.freq_long + " output from the HBV model in the period " + str(
1161                plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4],
1162                         size=14)
1163        else:
1164            fig.suptitle(parameter.freq_long + " output from the HBV model in the period " + str(
1165                plot_data.index.values[0])[
1166                                                                                             :4] + "-" + str(
1167                plot_data.index.values[-1])[:4], size=14)
1168        plt.tight_layout()
1169        fig.set_size_inches(10, 6)
1170        return fig
1171
1172    plot_data, plot_data_annual = plot_data(output_MATILDA, parameter)
1173    fig1 = plot_meteo(plot_data, parameter)
1174    fig2 = plot_runoff(plot_data, plot_data_annual, parameter)
1175    fig3 = plot_hbv(plot_data, parameter)
1176    output_MATILDA.extend([fig1, fig2, fig3])
1177    return output_MATILDA

1217        output_MATILDA[7].savefig(output_path + "HBV_output_" + str(output_MATILDA[0].index.values[-1])[:4] + ".png",
1218                                  dpi=output_MATILDA[7].dpi)
1219    else:
1220        output_MATILDA[7].savefig(
1221            output_path + "HBV_output_" + str(output_MATILDA[0].index.values[1])[:4] + "-" + str(
1222                output_MATILDA[0].index.values[-1])[:4] + ".png",
1223            dpi=output_MATILDA[7].dpi)

1227def matilda_simulation(input_df, obs=None, glacier_profile=None, output=None, warn=False,
1228                       set_up_start=None, set_up_end=None, sim_start=None, sim_end=None, freq="D", lat=None,
1229                       soi=None, area_cat=None, area_glac=None, ele_dat=None, ele_glac=None, ele_cat=None,
1230                       plots=True, hydro_year=10, parameter_df = None, lr_temp=-0.006, lr_prec=0, TT_snow=0,
1231                       TT_diff=2, CFMAX_snow=2.8, CFMAX_rel=2, BETA=1.0, CET=0.15,
1232                       FC=250, K0=0.055, K1=0.055, K2=0.04, LP=0.7, MAXBAS=3.0, PERC=1.5, UZL=120, PCORR=1.0, SFCF=0.7,
1233                       CWH=0.1, AG=0.7, RHO_snow=400):
1234    """Function to run the whole MATILDA simulation at once."""
1235
1236    print('---')
1237    print('MATILDA framework')
1238    parameter = matilda_parameter(input_df, set_up_start=set_up_start, set_up_end=set_up_end, sim_start=sim_start,
1239                                  sim_end=sim_end, freq=freq, lat=lat, area_cat=area_cat, area_glac=area_glac, ele_dat=ele_dat, \
1240                                  ele_glac=ele_glac, ele_cat=ele_cat, hydro_year=hydro_year, parameter_df = parameter_df, lr_temp=lr_temp,
1241                                  lr_prec=lr_prec, TT_snow=TT_snow, soi=soi, warn=warn, \
1242                                  TT_diff=TT_diff, CFMAX_snow=CFMAX_snow, CFMAX_rel=CFMAX_rel, \
1243                                  BETA=BETA, CET=CET, FC=FC, K0=K0, K1=K1, K2=K2, LP=LP, \
1244                                  MAXBAS=MAXBAS, PERC=PERC, UZL=UZL, PCORR=PCORR, SFCF=SFCF, CWH=CWH, AG=AG, RHO_snow=RHO_snow)
1245
1246    if parameter is None:
1247        return
1248
1249    # Data preprocessing with the MATILDA preparation script
1250    if obs is None:
1251        df_preproc = matilda_preproc(input_df, parameter)
1252        # Downscaling of data if necessary and the MATILDA simulation
1253        if glacier_profile is not None:
1254            output_MATILDA = matilda_submodules(df_preproc, parameter, glacier_profile=glacier_profile)
1255        else:
1256            output_MATILDA = matilda_submodules(df_preproc, parameter)
1257    else:
1258        df_preproc, obs_preproc = matilda_preproc(input_df, parameter, obs=obs)
1259        # Scale data if necessary and run the MATILDA simulation
1260        if glacier_profile is not None:
1261            output_MATILDA = matilda_submodules(df_preproc, parameter, obs=obs_preproc, glacier_profile=glacier_profile)
1262        else:
1263            output_MATILDA = matilda_submodules(df_preproc, parameter, obs=obs_preproc)
1264
1265    if plots:
1266        output_MATILDA = matilda_plots(output_MATILDA, parameter)   # Option to suppress plots.
1267        # return output_MATILDA
1268    else:
1269        return output_MATILDA
1270    # Creating plot for the input (meteorological) data (fig1), MATILDA runoff simulation (fig2) and HBV variables (fig3) and
1271    # adding them to the output
1272    # saving the data on disc of output path is given
1273    if output is not None:
1274        matilda_save_output(output_MATILDA, parameter, output)
1275
1276    return output_MATILDA

   1# -*- coding: UTF-8 -*-
   2"""
   3MATILDA Calibration Module "mspot"
   4--------------------------
   5This script provides tools for calibrating the MATILDA glacio-hydrological model using statistical parameter optimization
   6techniques. It makes extensive use of the SPOTPY package for sampling, optimization, and parameter uncertainty analysis. The module
   7is tailored for glacierized catchments and includes support for both catchment-wide and glacier-only calibration.
   8
   9Key Features:
  10-------------
  11- Parameter Sampling: Flexible setup for sampling hydrological model parameters using various algorithms from SPOTPY.
  12- Objective Functions: Includes multiple objective functions such as Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Mean Absolute Error
  13  (MAE), and custom user-defined functions.
  14- Calibration Targets: Supports calibration against observed discharge, glacier mass balance, and snow water equivalent.
  15- Statistical Analysis: Provides tools to analyze parameter posterior distributions and derive parameter bounds.
  16- Seasonal and Annual Analysis: Includes functions for evaluating seasonal (winter/summer) and annual metrics.
  17- Parallel Computing: Supports parallel sampling for computational efficiency.
  18
  19Functions:
  20----------
  211. `yesno`: Interactive function to confirm actions.
  222. `dict2bounds`: Converts a dictionary of parameter values into bounds.
  233. `loglike_kge`: Calculates a pseudo-log-likelihood using the Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE).
  244. `winter`, `summer`, `annual`: Extract seasonal or annual data slices for evaluation.
  255. `scaled_pdd`, `scaled_ndd`: Apply temperature lapse rates to calculate positive or negative degree days.
  266. `spot_setup` and `spot_setup_glacier`: Set up SPOTPY sampling for catchment-wide and glacier-specific calibration.
  277. `analyze_results`: Analyze SPOTPY results to identify the best-performing parameter set and generate diagnostic plots.
  288. `psample`: Automates parameter sampling and optimization with various SPOTPY algorithms.
  299. `load_parameters`: Loads the best-performing parameter set from SPOTPY results.
  3010. `get_par_bounds`: Derives parameter bounds from SPOTPY sampling results.
  31
  32Reference:
  33-----------
  34SPOTPY Library:
  35   - Houska, T., Kraft, P., Chamorro-Chavez, A., & Breuer, L. (2015). "SPOTting Model Parameters Using a Ready-Made
  36     Python Package." PLOS ONE, 10(12), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0145180
  37   - GitHub repository: https://github.com/thouska/spotpy
  38
  39Dependencies
  40------------
  41- Python 3.7 or higher
  42- spotpy
  43- pandas
  44- numpy
  45- matplotlib
  46- hydroeval
  47- scipy
  48
  49Usage:
  50------
  51This script is designed to be part of the MATILDA framework as calibration tool for the matilda.core model.
  52
  53License:

  61- Email: phillip.schuster@geo.hu-berlin.de
  62- Institution: Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin

  86class HiddenPrints:
  87    """
  88    Suppress prints during multiple iterations or noisy function calls.
  89
  90    This utility class redirects standard output to `/dev/null`, effectively silencing
  91    any print statements during its usage. It can be used as a context manager to suppress
  92    output temporarily.
  93
  94    Example:
  95        with HiddenPrints():
  96            # Any print statements here will be suppressed
  97            noisy_function()
  98
  99    Methods
 100    -------
 101    __enter__()
 102        Redirects standard output to `/dev/null`.
 103    __exit__(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb)
 104        Restores the original standard output.
 105    """
 106
 107    def __init__(self):
 108        # Initialize the attribute in the constructor
 109        self._original_stdout = None
 110
 111    def __enter__(self):
 112        self._original_stdout = sys.stdout
 113        sys.stdout = open(os.devnull, "w", encoding="utf-8")
 114
 115    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
 116        if sys.stdout:
 117            sys.stdout.close()
 118        sys.stdout = self._original_stdout

 121def yesno(question):
 122    """
 123    Prompt the user with a yes/no question and return the response.
 124
 125    This function repeatedly prompts the user with the given question until a valid
 126    response ('y' or 'n') is entered.
 127
 128    Parameters
 129    ----------
 130    question : str
 131        The yes/no question to present to the user.
 132
 133    Returns
 134    -------
 135    bool
 136        Returns True if the user responds with 'y', and False if the user responds with 'n'.
 137    """
 138
 139    prompt = f"{question} ? (y/n): "
 140    ans = input(prompt).strip().lower()
 141    if ans not in ["y", "n"]:
 142        print(f"{ans} is invalid, please try again...")
 143        return yesno(question)
 144    if ans == "y":
 145        return True
 146    return False

 149def dict2bounds(p_dict, drop=None):
 150    """
 151    Convert a parameter dictionary to a bounds dictionary to be passed to spot_setup().
 152
 153    This function takes a dictionary of parameters and converts it into a dictionary
 154    containing both lower (`_lo`) and upper (`_up`) bounds for each parameter. Optionally,
 155    specific parameters can be excluded from the resulting dictionary.
 156
 157    Parameters
 158    ----------
 159    p_dict : dict
 160        A dictionary containing parameter names as keys and their initial values as values.
 161    drop : list, optional
 162        A list of parameter names to exclude from the resulting bounds dictionary.
 163
 164    Returns
 165    -------
 166    dict
 167        A dictionary containing both lower (`_lo`) and upper (`_up`) bounds for the remaining
 168        parameters in `p_dict`.
 169    """
 170    if drop is None:
 171        drop = []
 172
 173    for i in drop:
 174        p_dict.pop(i, None)  # Use pop to avoid KeyError if key doesn't exist
 175
 176    p = {
 177        **dict(zip([i + "_lo" for i in p_dict.keys()], p_dict.values())),
 178        **dict(zip([i + "_up" for i in p_dict.keys()], p_dict.values())),
 179    }
 180    return p
 181

 183def loglike_kge(qsim, qobs):
 184    """
 185    Calculate a pseudo log-likelihood function using the Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) and a gamma distribution.
 186
 187    This function computes a log-likelihood value based on the KGE between simulated and observed flow values,
 188    and models the exceedance deviation (ED) using a gamma distribution.
 189
 190    Parameters
 191    ----------
 192    qsim : array_like
 193        Array of simulated flow values.
 194    qobs : array_like
 195        Array of observed flow values.
 196
 197    Returns
 198    -------
 199    float
 200        The calculated value of the log-likelihood function.
 201
 202    Notes
 203    -----
 204    The log-likelihood function is based on the Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) following Liu et al. (2022).
 205    The exceedance deviation (ED) is derived from the KGE as `ED = 1 - KGE`. The gamma probability density
 206    function (PDF) is then used to model the likelihood, with shape parameter `a=0.5` and scale parameter `scale=1`.
 207
 208    References
 209    ----------
 210    - Liu, Y., Fernández-Ortega, J., Mudarra, M., and Hartmann, A. (2022). "Pitfalls and a feasible solution for
 211      using KGE as an informal likelihood function in MCMC methods: DREAM(ZS) as an example." HESS, 26(20).
 212    - Kling, H., Gupta, H., & Yilmaz, K. K. (2012). "Model selection criteria for rainfall-runoff
 213      models: Representation of variability in Bayesian Model Averaging." Water Resources Research, 48(6), W06306.
 214    - `hydroeval`: https://github.com/ThibHlln/hydroeval
 215    - `scipy.stats.gamma`: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.gamma.html
 216    """
 217
 218    # Calculate KGE
 219    n = len(qobs)
 220    KGE = he.kge_2012(qsim, qobs, remove_zero=True)
 221    ED = 1 - KGE
 222
 223    # Calculate log-likelihood function
 224    gammapdf = gamma.pdf(ED, a=0.5, scale=1)
 225    log_L = 0.5 * n * np.log(gammapdf)
 226
 227    return log_L
 228

 230def winter(year, data):
 231    """
 232    Extract the winter period for a given year from a record of the World Glacier Monitoring service (WGMS).
 233
 234    This function filters the input dataset for the specified year and returns a slice object representing the winter
 235    period based on the `BEGIN_PERIOD` and `END_WINTER` columns.
 236
 237    Parameters
 238    ----------
 239    year : int
 240        The year for which the winter period is to be extracted.
 241    data : pandas.DataFrame
 242        The input dataset containing at least the following columns:
 243        - `BEGIN_PERIOD`: The start of the winter period.
 244        - `END_WINTER`: The end of the winter period.
 245        - Index representing years.
 246
 247    Returns
 248    -------
 249    slice
 250        A slice object representing the winter period for the specified year.
 251
 252    Notes
 253    -----
 254    The function assumes that the dataset is indexed by years and contains the `BEGIN_PERIOD` and `END_WINTER` columns
 255    with appropriate datetime or timestamp values.
 256
 257    References
 258    ----------
 259    - WGMS (2024): Fluctuations of Glaciers Database. World Glacier Monitoring Service, Zurich, Switzerland.
 260    https://doi.org/10.5904/wgms-fog-2024-01
 261    """
 262
 263    data = data[data.index == year]
 264    winter_slice = slice(data.BEGIN_PERIOD.squeeze(), data.END_WINTER.squeeze())
 265    return winter_slice
 266
 267

 344def scaled_pdd(data, elev, lr):
 345    """
 346    Calculate scaled positive degree days (PDD) based on temperature lapse rate and elevation adjustments.
 347
 348    This function adjusts the input temperature data for elevation differences using a given lapse rate, then calculates
 349    the positive degree days by setting all negative or zero temperatures to zero.
 350
 351    Parameters
 352    ----------
 353    data : array_like
 354        Array or series of temperature values (in °C).
 355    elev : float
 356        Elevation difference (in meters) used for scaling the temperature values.
 357    lr : float
 358        Temperature lapse rate (in °C/m) used for scaling.
 359
 360    Returns
 361    -------
 362    pdd : array_like
 363        Scaled positive degree days (PDD), where negative values are replaced with zero.
 364
 365    Notes
 366    -----
 367    Positive degree days are commonly used in snow and ice melt models to estimate melt based on temperature inputs.
 368    This function adjusts the temperature for elevation differences before computing PDD.
 369
 370    Examples
 371    --------
 372    >>> data = np.array([2, -1, 3, -2, 5])
 373    >>> elev = 500  # meters
 374    >>> lr = -0.006  # °C/m
 375    >>> scaled_pdd(data, elev, lr)
 376    array([5, 0, 6, 0, 8])
 377    """
 378
 379    s = data + elev * lr
 380    pdd = np.where(s > 0, s, 0)
 381    return pdd
 382
 383
 384def scaled_ndd(data, elev, lr):
 385    """
 386    Calculate scaled negative degree days (NDD) based on temperature lapse rate and elevation adjustments.
 387
 388    This function adjusts the input temperature data for elevation differences using a given lapse rate, then calculates
 389    the negative degree days by setting all positive or zero temperatures to zero and marking negative temperatures as 1.
 390
 391    Parameters
 392    ----------
 393    data : array_like
 394        Array or series of temperature values (in °C).
 395    elev : float
 396        Elevation difference (in meters) used for scaling the temperature values.
 397    lr : float
 398        Temperature lapse rate (in °C/m) used for scaling.
 399
 400    Returns
 401    -------
 402    ndd : array_like
 403        Scaled negative degree days (NDD), where negative temperatures are marked as 1 and others as 0.
 404
 405    Notes
 406    -----
 407    Negative degree days are used in some hydrological and glaciological models to track periods with freezing conditions.
 408    This function adjusts the temperature for elevation differences before computing NDD.
 409
 410    Examples
 411    --------
 412    >>> data = np.array([2, -1, 3, -2, 5])
 413    >>> elev = 500  # meters
 414    >>> lr = -0.006  # °C/m
 415    >>> scaled_ndd(data, elev, lr)
 416    array([0, 1, 0, 1, 0])
 417    """
 418
 419    s = data + elev * lr
 420    ndd = np.where(s < 0, 1, 0)
 421    return ndd
 422

 424def spot_setup(
 425    set_up_start=None,
 426    set_up_end=None,
 427    sim_start=None,
 428    sim_end=None,
 429    freq="D",
 430    lat=None,
 431    area_cat=None,
 432    area_glac=None,
 433    ele_dat=None,
 434    ele_glac=None,
 435    ele_cat=None,
 436    glacier_profile=None,
 437    elev_rescaling=True,
 438    target_mb=None,
 439    target_swe=None,
 440    swe_scaling=None,
 441    fix_param=None,
 442    fix_val=None,
 443    obj_func=None,
 444    lr_temp_lo=-0.0065,
 445    lr_temp_up=-0.0055,
 446    lr_prec_lo=0,
 447    lr_prec_up=0.002,
 448    BETA_lo=1,
 449    BETA_up=6,
 450    CET_lo=0,
 451    CET_up=0.3,
 452    FC_lo=50,
 453    FC_up=500,
 454    K0_lo=0.01,
 455    K0_up=0.4,
 456    K1_lo=0.01,
 457    K1_up=0.4,
 458    K2_lo=0.001,
 459    K2_up=0.15,
 460    LP_lo=0.3,
 461    LP_up=1,
 462    MAXBAS_lo=2,
 463    MAXBAS_up=7,
 464    PERC_lo=0,
 465    PERC_up=3,
 466    UZL_lo=0,
 467    UZL_up=500,
 468    PCORR_lo=0.5,
 469    PCORR_up=2,
 470    TT_snow_lo=-1.5,
 471    TT_snow_up=1.5,
 472    TT_diff_lo=0.5,
 473    TT_diff_up=2.5,
 474    CFMAX_snow_lo=0.5,
 475    CFMAX_snow_up=10,
 476    CFMAX_rel_lo=1.2,
 477    CFMAX_rel_up=2,
 478    SFCF_lo=0.4,
 479    SFCF_up=1,
 480    CWH_lo=0,
 481    CWH_up=0.2,
 482    AG_lo=0,
 483    AG_up=1,
 484    CFR_lo=0.05,
 485    CFR_up=0.25,
 486    interf=4,
 487    freqst=2,
 488):
 489    """
 490    Spotpy-based setup for parameter optimization and calibration of the MATILDA model.
 491
 492    This class provides the framework to optimize the parameters of the MATILDA model using SPOTPY, a statistical parameter
 493    optimization tool. It enables flexible parameter setup, handles fixed parameters, and evaluates simulation results
 494    against observed data (e.g., streamflow, snow water equivalent, surface mass balance).
 495
 496    Parameters
 497    ----------
 498    General inputs:
 499    - set_up_start, set_up_end : str
 500        Start and end dates of the setup period.
 501    - sim_start, sim_end : str
 502        Start and end dates of the simulation period.
 503    - freq : str, optional
 504        Frequency of the data, default is daily ("D").
 505    - lat : float, optional
 506        Latitude of the catchment for extraterrestrial radiation calculation.
 507    - area_cat, area_glac : float
 508        Catchment and glacierized areas in km².
 509    - ele_dat, ele_glac, ele_cat : float
 510        Mean elevations (m a.s.l.) of the data, glacier, and catchment.
 511    - glacier_profile : DataFrame, optional
 512        Glacier profile for scaling and elevation rescaling.
 513    - elev_rescaling : bool, optional
 514        Flag for enabling elevation rescaling, default is True.
 515    - target_mb, target_swe : float, optional
 516        Target surface mass balance (MB) or snow water equivalent (SWE) for calibration.
 517    - swe_scaling : float, optional
 518        Scaling factor for snow water equivalent. Used to account for the mismatch in resolution of the SWE calibration
 519        data and the glacier mask used for MATILDA.
 520
 521    Parameter bounds for calibration:
 522    - Fix parameter bounds (e.g., `lr_temp_lo`, `lr_temp_up` for lapse rates).
 523    - `fix_param` : list, optional
 524        List of parameters to fix during calibration.
 525    - `fix_val` : dict, optional
 526        Fixed parameter values (if applicable).
 527
 528    SPOTPY settings:
 529    - `interf` : int, optional
 530        Inference factor for parameter iterations, default is 4.
 531    - `freqst` : int, optional
 532        Frequency step for sensitivity analysis, default is 2.
 533
 534    Methods
 535    -------
 536    simulation(x, param_names, fix_param, fix_val, swe_scaling)
 537        Executes the MATILDA simulation with sampled parameters and fixed parameters (if specified).
 538    evaluation()
 539        Prepares the observed data (e.g., streamflow, SWE) for comparison with simulation results.
 540    objectivefunction(simulation, evaluation, params=None)
 541        Defines the objective function for model evaluation using the Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) or user-defined metrics.
 542
 543    Returns
 544    -------
 545    spot_setup_class : class
 546        Configured SPOTPY setup class for MATILDA parameter optimization and calibration.
 547
 548    References
 549    ----------
 550    - SPOTPY library:
 551      - Houska, T., Kraft, P., Chamorro-Chavez, A., & Breuer, L. (2015). "SPOTting Model Parameters Using a Ready-Made
 552        Python Package." PLOS ONE, 10(12), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0145180
 553      - GitHub repository: https://github.com/thouska/spotpy
 554
 555    - Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE):
 556      - Gupta, H. V., & Kling, H. (2011). "On typical range, sensitivity, and normalization of Mean Squared Error and
 557        Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency type metrics." Water Resources Research, 47(10). https://doi.org/10.1029/2011WR010962
 558      - Kling, H., Fuchs, M., & Paulin, M. (2012). "Runoff conditions in the upper Danube basin under an ensemble of
 559        climate change scenarios." Journal of Hydrology, 424-425, 264-277. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2012.01.011
 560    """
 561
 562    class spot_setup_class:
 563        """
 564        spot_setup_class: A SPOTPY setup class for MATILDA model parameter calibration.
 565
 566        This class is designed to facilitate the optimization and calibration of the MATILDA model parameters
 567        using SPOTPY, a statistical parameter optimization library. It defines the parameter space, simulation
 568        methods, evaluation functions, and the objective function to assess the model's performance.
 569
 570        Attributes
 571        ----------
 572        param : list
 573            List of SPOTPY parameter distributions for calibration.
 574        param_names : list
 575            List of names corresponding to the parameters being calibrated.
 576        par_iter : int
 577            Number of parameter iterations needed for sensitivity analysis and parameter inference.
 578
 579        Methods
 580        -------
 581        __init__(df, obs, swe, obj_func=None)
 582            Initializes the setup class with input data, observations, and an optional objective function.
 583
 584        simulation(x, param_names=param_names, fix_param=fix_param, fix_val=fix_val, swe_scaling=swe_scaling)
 585            Runs the MATILDA simulation with sampled parameters and any fixed parameters specified.
 586
 587        evaluation()
 588            Prepares the observed data (e.g., streamflow, snow water equivalent, surface mass balance) for
 589            comparison with simulation results.
 590
 591        objectivefunction(simulation, evaluation, params=None)
 592            Calculates the objective function to evaluate model performance. Supports metrics such as
 593            the Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) and custom metrics defined by the user.
 594
 595        Usage
 596        -----
 597        The `spot_setup_class` is instantiated with observed data (`obs`) and optionally with snow water equivalent
 598        (SWE) data and a custom objective function. Once instantiated, it can be passed to SPOTPY's optimization
 599        and sensitivity analysis tools to calibrate the MATILDA model.
 600
 601        Example
 602        -------
 603        from spotpy.algorithms import sceua
 604        spot_setup_instance = spot_setup(df, obs, swe, obj_func)
 605        sampler = sceua(spot_setup_instance)
 606        sampler.sample(1000)
 607
 608        References
 609        ----------
 610        - SPOTPY library:
 611          - Houska, T., et al. (2015). "SPOTting Model Parameters Using a Ready-Made Python Package." PLOS ONE.
 612          - GitHub: https://github.com/thouska/spotpy
 613
 614        - Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE):
 615          - Gupta, H. V., & Kling, H. (2011). "On typical range, sensitivity, and normalization of Mean Squared Error
 616            and Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency type metrics." Water Resources Research.
 617          - Kling, H., et al. (2012). "Runoff conditions in the upper Danube basin under an ensemble of climate
 618            change scenarios." Journal of Hydrology.
 619        """
 620
 621        # defining all parameters and the distribution
 622        lr_temp = Uniform(low=lr_temp_lo, high=lr_temp_up)
 623        lr_prec = Uniform(low=lr_prec_lo, high=lr_prec_up)
 624        BETA = Uniform(low=BETA_lo, high=BETA_up)
 625        CET = Uniform(low=CET_lo, high=CET_up)
 626        FC = Uniform(low=FC_lo, high=FC_up)
 627        K0 = Uniform(low=K0_lo, high=K0_up)
 628        K1 = Uniform(low=K1_lo, high=K1_up)
 629        K2 = Uniform(low=K2_lo, high=K2_up)
 630        LP = Uniform(low=LP_lo, high=LP_up)
 631        MAXBAS = Uniform(low=MAXBAS_lo, high=MAXBAS_up)
 632        PERC = Uniform(low=PERC_lo, high=PERC_up)
 633        UZL = Uniform(low=UZL_lo, high=UZL_up)
 634        PCORR = Uniform(low=PCORR_lo, high=PCORR_up)
 635        TT_snow = Uniform(low=TT_snow_lo, high=TT_snow_up)
 636        TT_diff = Uniform(low=TT_diff_lo, high=TT_diff_up)
 637        CFMAX_snow = Uniform(low=CFMAX_snow_lo, high=CFMAX_snow_up)
 638        CFMAX_rel = Uniform(low=CFMAX_rel_lo, high=CFMAX_rel_up)
 639        SFCF = Uniform(low=SFCF_lo, high=SFCF_up)
 640        CWH = Uniform(low=CWH_lo, high=CWH_up)
 641        AG = Uniform(low=AG_lo, high=AG_up)
 642        CFR = Uniform(low=CFR_lo, high=CFR_up)
 643
 644        # Create the list containing the variables
 645        param = [
 646            lr_temp,
 647            lr_prec,
 648            BETA,
 649            CET,
 650            FC,
 651            K0,
 652            K1,
 653            K2,
 654            LP,
 655            MAXBAS,
 656            PERC,
 657            UZL,
 658            PCORR,
 659            TT_snow,
 660            TT_diff,
 661            CFMAX_snow,
 662            CFMAX_rel,
 663            SFCF,
 664            CWH,
 665            AG,
 666            CFR,
 667        ]
 668
 669        # Exclude parameters defined in fix_param
 670        param_names = [
 671            "lr_temp",
 672            "lr_prec",
 673            "BETA",
 674            "CET",
 675            "FC",
 676            "K0",
 677            "K1",
 678            "K2",
 679            "LP",
 680            "MAXBAS",
 681            "PERC",
 682            "UZL",
 683            "PCORR",
 684            "TT_snow",
 685            "TT_diff",
 686            "CFMAX_snow",
 687            "CFMAX_rel",
 688            "SFCF",
 689            "CWH",
 690            "AG",
 691            "CFR",
 692        ]
 693
 694        # Exclude parameters that should be fixed
 695        if fix_param:
 696            param = [p for p, name in zip(param, param_names) if name not in fix_param]
 697            param_names = [param for param in param_names if param not in fix_param]
 698            for par in fix_param:
 699                if par in globals():
 700                    del globals()[par]
 701                if par in locals():
 702                    del locals()[par]
 703
 704        # Number of needed parameter iterations for parametrization and sensitivity analysis
 705        M = interf  # inference factor (default = 4)
 706        d = freqst  # frequency step (default = 2)
 707        k = len(param)  # number of parameters
 708
 709        par_iter = (1 + 4 * M**2 * (1 + (k - 2) * d)) * k
 710
 711        def __init__(
 712            self,
 713            df,
 714            obs,
 715            swe,
 716            swe_scaling=swe_scaling,
 717            fix_param=fix_param,
 718            fix_val=fix_val,
 719            obj_func=obj_func,
 720        ):
 721            self.obj_func = obj_func
 722            self.Input = df
 723            self.obs = obs
 724            self.swe = swe
 725            self.swe_scaling = swe_scaling
 726            self.fix_param = fix_param
 727            self.fix_val = fix_val
 728
 729        def simulation(self, x, param_names=None):
 730            if param_names is None:
 731                param_names = self.param_names
 732
 733            with HiddenPrints():
 734                # Setup all parameters for sampling
 735                args = {par_name: x[par_name] for par_name in param_names}
 736
 737                # Fix parameters on desired values if defined
 738                if self.fix_param is not None and self.fix_val is not None:
 739                    for p in self.fix_param:
 740                        if p in self.fix_val:
 741                            args[p] = self.fix_val[p]
 742
 743                sim = matilda_simulation(
 744                    self.Input,
 745                    obs=self.obs,
 746                    output=None,
 747                    set_up_start=set_up_start,
 748                    set_up_end=set_up_end,
 749                    sim_start=sim_start,
 750                    sim_end=sim_end,
 751                    freq=freq,
 752                    lat=lat,
 753                    area_cat=area_cat,
 754                    area_glac=area_glac,
 755                    ele_dat=ele_dat,
 756                    ele_glac=ele_glac,
 757                    ele_cat=ele_cat,
 758                    plots=False,
 759                    warn=False,
 760                    glacier_profile=glacier_profile,
 761                    elev_rescaling=elev_rescaling,
 762                    **args,
 763                )
 764                swe_sim = (
 765                    sim[0]
 766                    .snowpack_off_glaciers["2000-01-01":"2017-09-30"]
 767                    .to_frame(name="SWE_sim")
 768                )
 769                if self.swe_scaling is not None:
 770                    swe_sim = swe_sim * self.swe_scaling
 771
 772            if target_mb is None:
 773                if target_swe is None:
 774                    return sim[0].total_runoff
 775                return [sim[0].total_runoff, swe_sim.SWE_sim]
 776
 777            if target_swe is None:
 778                return [sim[0].total_runoff, sim[5].smb_water_year.mean()]
 779            return [
 780                sim[0].total_runoff,
 781                sim[5].smb_water_year.mean(),
 782                swe_sim.SWE_sim,
 783            ]
 784
 785        def evaluation(self):
 786            obs_preproc = self.obs.copy()
 787            obs_preproc.set_index("Date", inplace=True)
 788            obs_preproc.index = pd.to_datetime(obs_preproc.index)
 789            obs_preproc = obs_preproc[sim_start:sim_end]
 790            # Changing the input unit from m³/s to mm.
 791            obs_preproc["Qobs"] = (
 792                obs_preproc["Qobs"] * 86400 / (area_cat * 1000000) * 1000
 793            )
 794            # To daily resolution
 795            obs_preproc = obs_preproc.resample("D").agg(pd.Series.sum, skipna=False)
 796            # Expanding the observation period full years filling up with NAs
 797            idx_first = obs_preproc.index.year[1]
 798            idx_last = obs_preproc.index.year[-1]
 799            idx = pd.date_range(
 800                start=date(idx_first, 1, 1),
 801                end=date(idx_last, 12, 31),
 802                freq="D",
 803                name=obs_preproc.index.name,
 804            )
 805            obs_preproc = obs_preproc.reindex(idx)
 806            obs_preproc = obs_preproc.fillna(np.NaN)
 807
 808            if target_swe is not None:
 809                swe_obs = self.swe
 810                if "Date" in self.swe.columns:
 811                    swe_obs["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(swe_obs["Date"])
 812                    swe_obs.set_index("Date", inplace=True)
 813                swe_obs = swe_obs * 1000
 814                swe_obs = swe_obs["2000-01-01":"2017-09-30"]
 815
 816            if target_mb is None:
 817                if target_swe is None:
 818                    return obs_preproc.Qobs
 819                return [obs_preproc.Qobs, swe_obs.SWE_Mean]
 820
 821            if target_swe is None:
 822                return [obs_preproc.Qobs, target_mb]
 823            return [obs_preproc.Qobs, target_mb, swe_obs.SWE_Mean]
 824
 825        def objectivefunction(self, simulation, evaluation):
 826            # SPOTPY expects to get one or multiple values back,
 827            # that define the performance of the model run
 828            if target_mb is not None:
 829                if target_swe is not None:
 830                    sim_runoff, sim_smb, sim_swe = simulation
 831                    eval_runoff, eval_smb, eval_swe = evaluation
 832                    obj3 = he.kge_2012(sim_swe, eval_swe, remove_zero=False)
 833                else:
 834                    sim_runoff, sim_smb = simulation
 835                    eval_runoff, eval_smb = evaluation
 836
 837                obj2 = abs(eval_smb - sim_smb)
 838                simulation = sim_runoff
 839                evaluation = eval_runoff
 840
 841            elif target_swe is not None:
 842                sim_runoff, sim_swe = simulation
 843                eval_runoff, eval_swe = evaluation
 844                obj3 = he.kge_2012(sim_swe, eval_swe, remove_zero=False)
 845
 846            # Crop both timeseries to same periods without NAs
 847            sim_new = pd.DataFrame()
 848            sim_new["mod"] = pd.DataFrame(simulation)
 849            sim_new["obs"] = evaluation
 850            clean = sim_new.dropna()
 851
 852            simulation_clean = clean["mod"]
 853            evaluation_clean = clean["obs"]
 854
 855            if not self.obj_func:
 856                # This is used if not overwritten by user
 857                # obj1 = kge(evaluation_clean, simulation_clean)          # SPOTPY internal kge
 858                obj1 = he.kge_2012(
 859                    simulation_clean, evaluation_clean, remove_zero=True
 860                )  # same as MATILDA
 861            else:
 862                # Way to ensure flexible spot setup class
 863                obj1 = self.obj_func(evaluation_clean, simulation_clean)
 864
 865            if target_mb is None:
 866                if target_swe is None:
 867                    return obj1
 868                return [obj1, obj3]
 869
 870            if target_swe is None:
 871                return [obj1, obj2]
 872
 873            return [obj1, obj2, obj3]
 874
 875    return spot_setup_class
 876
 877
 878def spot_setup_glacier(
 879    set_up_start=None,
 880    set_up_end=None,
 881    sim_start=None,
 882    sim_end=None,
 883    freq="D",
 884    lat=None,
 885    area_cat=None,
 886    area_glac=None,
 887    ele_dat=None,
 888    ele_glac=None,
 889    glacier_profile=None,
 890    obs_type="annual",
 891    obj_func=None,
 892    lr_temp_lo=-0.0065,
 893    lr_temp_up=-0.0055,
 894    lr_prec_lo=0,
 895    lr_prec_up=0.002,
 896    PCORR_lo=0.5,
 897    PCORR_up=2,
 898    TT_snow_lo=-1.5,
 899    TT_snow_up=1.5,
 900    TT_diff_lo=0.5,
 901    TT_diff_up=2.5,
 902    CFMAX_snow_lo=0.5,
 903    CFMAX_snow_up=10,
 904    CFMAX_rel_lo=1.2,
 905    CFMAX_rel_up=2,
 906    SFCF_lo=0.4,
 907    SFCF_up=1,
 908    CFR_lo=0.05,
 909    CFR_up=0.25,
 910    interf=4,
 911    freqst=2,
 912):
 913    """
 914    Spotpy-based setup for parameter optimization and calibration of the MATILDA model for a (sub-)catchment entirely
 915    covered by glaciers.
 916
 917    This class provides the framework to optimize the parameters of the MATILDA model using SPOTPY, a statistical parameter
 918    optimization tool. It enables flexible parameter setup, handles fixed parameters, and evaluates simulation results
 919    against observed data (e.g., streamflow, snow water equivalent, surface mass balance). It supports annual, winter,
 920    and summer mass balance optimization based on observed data.
 921
 922    Parameters
 923    ----------
 924    General inputs:
 925    - set_up_start, set_up_end : str
 926        Start and end dates of the setup period.
 927    - sim_start, sim_end : str
 928        Start and end dates of the simulation period.
 929    - freq : str, optional
 930        Frequency of the data, default is daily ("D").
 931    - lat : float, optional
 932        Latitude of the catchment for extraterrestrial radiation calculation.
 933    - area_cat, area_glac : float
 934        Catchment and glacierized areas in km².
 935    - ele_dat, ele_glac, ele_cat : float
 936        Mean elevations (m a.s.l.) of the data, glacier, and catchment.
 937    - glacier_profile : DataFrame
 938        Glacier profile used for elevation rescaling and look-up table generation.
 939    - obs_type : str, optional
 940        Type of observed mass balance data: "annual", "winter", or "summer". Default is "annual".
 941    - obj_func : callable, optional
 942        Custom objective function to compare simulation and observation. If None, the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is used.
 943
 944    Parameter bounds for calibration:
 945    - lr_temp_lo, lr_temp_up : float
 946        Bounds for temperature lapse rate (°C/m).
 947    - lr_prec_lo, lr_prec_up : float
 948        Bounds for precipitation correction factor.
 949    - PCORR_lo, PCORR_up : float
 950        Bounds for precipitation correction factor.
 951    - TT_snow_lo, TT_snow_up : float
 952        Bounds for snow temperature threshold (°C).
 953    - TT_diff_lo, TT_diff_up : float
 954        Bounds for the difference between rain and snow temperature thresholds (°C).
 955    - CFMAX_snow_lo, CFMAX_snow_up : float
 956        Bounds for the degree-day factor for snow melt (mm/°C/day).
 957    - CFMAX_rel_lo, CFMAX_rel_up : float
 958        Bounds for the degree-day factor for relative snow and ice melt.
 959    - SFCF_lo, SFCF_up : float
 960        Bounds for snow correction factor.
 961    - CFR_lo, CFR_up : float
 962        Bounds for the refreezing factor.
 963
 964    SPOTPY settings:
 965    - interf : int, optional
 966        Inference factor for parameter iterations, default is 4.
 967    - freqst : int, optional
 968        Frequency step for sensitivity analysis, default is 2.
 969
 970    Methods
 971    -------
 972    simulation(x)
 973        Executes the glacier mass balance simulation using the degree-day model (DDM).
 974    evaluation()
 975        Prepares observed mass balance data (annual, winter, or summer) for comparison.
 976    objectivefunction(simulation, evaluation, params=None)
 977        Defines the objective function to calculate the error between simulated and observed mass balance values.
 978
 979    Returns
 980    -------
 981    spot_setup_class : class
 982        Configured SPOTPY setup class for glacier mass balance parameter optimization.
 983
 984    References
 985    ----------
 986    - SPOTPY library:
 987      - Houska, T., Kraft, P., Chamorro-Chavez, A., & Breuer, L. (2015). "SPOTting Model Parameters Using a Ready-Made
 988        Python Package." PLOS ONE, 10(12), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0145180
 989      - GitHub repository: https://github.com/thouska/spotpy
 990    """
 991
 992    class spot_setup_class:
 993        """
 994        spot_setup_class: A SPOTPY setup class for MATILDA model glacier mass balance parameter calibration.
 995
 996        This class facilitates the calibration and optimization of the MATILDA model parameters for glacier mass balance
 997        modeling. It uses SPOTPY, a statistical parameter optimization library, to define the parameter space, simulate
 998        mass balance, and evaluate the model's performance against observed data.
 999
1000        Attributes
1001        ----------
1002        param : list
1003            List of SPOTPY parameter distributions for calibration, including lapse rates, temperature thresholds, and
1004            degree-day factors.
1005        par_iter : int
1006            Number of parameter iterations needed for sensitivity analysis and parameter inference.
1007
1008        Methods
1009        -------
1010        __init__(df, obs, obj_func=None)
1011            Initializes the class with input data (`df`), observed data (`obs`), and an optional custom objective function.
1012
1013        simulation(x)
1014            Simulates glacier mass balance using the MATILDA model with the specified parameters.
1015
1016        evaluation()
1017            Processes the observed mass balance data into a format compatible with the simulated outputs.
1018
1019        objectivefunction(simulation, evaluation, params=None)
1020            Defines the objective function to evaluate the model's performance. By default, it uses the Mean Absolute
1021            Error (MAE) or a custom user-defined function.
1022
1023        Usage
1024        -----
1025        The `spot_setup_class` is instantiated with observed data and passed to SPOTPY for parameter optimization and
1026        sensitivity analysis.
1027
1028        Example
1029        -------
1030        from spotpy.algorithms import sceua
1031
1032        spot_setup_instance = spot_setup_glacier(df, obs, obj_func)
1033        sampler = sceua(spot_setup_instance)
1034        sampler.sample(1000)
1035
1036        Parameters
1037        ----------
1038        General Inputs:
1039        - set_up_start, set_up_end : str
1040            Start and end dates of the setup period.
1041        - sim_start, sim_end : str
1042            Start and end dates of the simulation period.
1043        - freq : str, optional
1044            Frequency of the data, default is daily ("D").
1045        - lat : float, optional
1046            Latitude of the catchment for extraterrestrial radiation calculation.
1047        - area_cat, area_glac : float
1048            Catchment and glacierized areas in km².
1049        - ele_dat, ele_glac, ele_cat : float
1050            Mean elevations (m a.s.l.) of the data, glacier, and catchment.
1051        - glacier_profile : DataFrame
1052            Glacier profile used for elevation rescaling and look-up table generation.
1053        - obs_type : str, optional
1054            Type of observed mass balance data ("annual", "winter", or "summer"). Default is "annual".
1055        - obj_func : callable, optional
1056            Custom objective function to compare simulation and observation. Defaults to Mean Absolute Error (MAE).
1057
1058        Parameter Bounds for Calibration:
1059        - lr_temp_lo, lr_temp_up : float
1060            Bounds for the temperature lapse rate (°C/m).
1061        - lr_prec_lo, lr_prec_up : float
1062            Bounds for the precipitation correction factor.
1063        - PCORR_lo, PCORR_up : float
1064            Bounds for the precipitation correction factor.
1065        - TT_snow_lo, TT_snow_up : float
1066            Bounds for the snow temperature threshold (°C).
1067        - TT_diff_lo, TT_diff_up : float
1068            Bounds for the difference between rain and snow temperature thresholds (°C).
1069        - CFMAX_snow_lo, CFMAX_snow_up : float
1070            Bounds for the degree-day factor for snow melt (mm/°C/day).
1071        - CFMAX_rel_lo, CFMAX_rel_up : float
1072            Bounds for the degree-day factor for relative snow and ice melt.
1073        - SFCF_lo, SFCF_up : float
1074            Bounds for the snow correction factor.
1075        - CFR_lo, CFR_up : float
1076            Bounds for the refreezing factor.
1077
1078        SPOTPY Settings:
1079        - interf : int, optional
1080            Inference factor for parameter iterations. Default is 4.
1081        - freqst : int, optional
1082            Frequency step for sensitivity analysis. Default is 2.
1083
1084        Returns
1085        -------
1086        spot_setup_class : class
1087            Configured SPOTPY setup class for glacier mass balance parameter optimization.
1088
1089        References
1090        ----------
1091        - SPOTPY library:
1092          - Houska, T., Kraft, P., Chamorro-Chavez, A., & Breuer, L. (2015). "SPOTting Model Parameters Using a Ready-Made
1093            Python Package." PLOS ONE, 10(12), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0145180
1094          - GitHub repository: https://github.com/thouska/spotpy
1095        """
1096
1097        # defining all parameters and the distribution
1098        param = (
1099            lr_temp,
1100            lr_prec,
1101            PCORR,
1102            TT_snow,
1103            TT_diff,
1104            CFMAX_snow,
1105            CFMAX_rel,
1106            SFCF,
1107            CFR,
1108        ) = [
1109            Uniform(low=lr_temp_lo, high=lr_temp_up),  # lr_temp
1110            Uniform(low=lr_prec_lo, high=lr_prec_up),  # lr_prec
1111            Uniform(low=PCORR_lo, high=PCORR_up),  # PCORR
1112            Uniform(low=TT_snow_lo, high=TT_snow_up),  # TT_snow
1113            Uniform(low=TT_diff_lo, high=TT_diff_up),  # TT_diff
1114            Uniform(low=CFMAX_snow_lo, high=CFMAX_snow_up),  # CFMAX_snow
1115            Uniform(low=CFMAX_rel_lo, high=CFMAX_rel_up),  # CFMAX_rel
1116            Uniform(low=SFCF_lo, high=SFCF_up),  # SFCF
1117            Uniform(low=CFR_lo, high=CFR_up),  # CFR
1118        ]
1119
1120        # Number of needed parameter iterations for parametrization and sensitivity analysis
1121        M = interf  # inference factor (default = 4)
1122        d = freqst  # frequency step (default = 2)
1123        k = len(param)  # number of parameters
1124
1125        par_iter = (1 + 4 * M**2 * (1 + (k - 2) * d)) * k
1126
1127        def __init__(self, df, obs, obj_func=obj_func):
1128            self.obj_func = obj_func
1129            self.Input = df
1130            self.obs = obs
1131
1132        def simulation(self, x):
1133            with HiddenPrints():
1134                parameter = matilda_parameter(
1135                    self.Input,
1136                    set_up_start=set_up_start,
1137                    set_up_end=set_up_end,
1138                    sim_start=sim_start,
1139                    sim_end=sim_end,
1140                    freq=freq,
1141                    lat=lat,
1142                    area_cat=area_cat,
1143                    area_glac=area_glac,
1144                    ele_dat=ele_dat,
1145                    ele_glac=ele_glac,
1146                    ele_cat=None,
1147                    lr_temp=x.lr_temp,
1148                    lr_prec=x.lr_prec,
1149                    PCORR=x.PCORR,
1150                    TT_snow=x.TT_snow,
1151                    TT_diff=x.TT_diff,
1152                    CFMAX_snow=x.CFMAX_snow,
1153                    CFMAX_rel=x.CFMAX_rel,
1154                    SFCF=x.SFCF,
1155                    CFR=x.CFR,
1156                )
1157
1158                df_preproc = matilda_preproc(self.Input, parameter)
1159                lookup_table = create_lookup_table(glacier_profile, parameter)
1160                output_DDM = updated_glacier_melt(
1161                    df_preproc, lookup_table, glacier_profile, parameter
1162                )[0]
1163                sim = output_DDM.DDM_smb
1164
1165            return sim
1166
1167        def evaluation(self):
1168            obs_preproc = self.obs.copy()
1169            obs_preproc.set_index("YEAR", inplace=True)
1170            obs_preproc.index = pd.to_datetime(obs_preproc.index)
1171
1172            return obs_preproc
1173
1174        def objectivefunction(self, simulation, evaluation):
1175            # Aggregate MBs to fit the calibration data
1176            sim = []
1177            obs = []
1178            sim_new = pd.DataFrame()
1179            if obs_type == "winter":
1180                for i in evaluation.index:
1181                    mb = simulation[winter(i, evaluation)].sum()
1182                    sim.append(mb)
1183                    mb_obs = evaluation[evaluation.index == i].WINTER_BALANCE.squeeze()
1184                    obs.append(mb_obs)
1185
1186            if obs_type == "summer":
1187                for i in evaluation.index:
1188                    mb = simulation[summer(i, evaluation)].sum()
1189                    sim.append(mb)
1190                    mb_obs = evaluation[evaluation.index == i].SUMMER_BALANCE.squeeze()
1191                    obs.append(mb_obs)
1192
1193            if obs_type == "annual":
1194                for i in evaluation.index:
1195                    mb_sim = simulation[annual(i, evaluation)].sum()
1196                    sim.append(mb_sim)
1197                    mb_obs = evaluation[evaluation.index == i].ANNUAL_BALANCE.squeeze()
1198                    obs.append(mb_obs)
1199
1200            # Crop both timeseries to same periods without NAs
1201            sim_new["mod"] = pd.DataFrame(sim)
1202            sim_new["obs"] = pd.DataFrame(obs)
1203
1204            clean = sim_new.dropna()
1205
1206            simulation_clean = clean["mod"]
1207            evaluation_clean = clean["obs"]
1208
1209            if not self.obj_func:
1210                # This is used if not overwritten by user
1211                like = mae(evaluation_clean, simulation_clean)
1212                print("MAE: " + str(like))
1213            else:
1214                # Way to ensure flexible spot setup class
1215                like = self.obj_func(evaluation_clean, simulation_clean)
1216            return like
1217
1218    return spot_setup_class
1219

1221def analyze_results(
1222    sampling_data,
1223    obs,
1224    algorithm,
1225    obj_dir="maximize",
1226    fig_path=None,
1227    dbname="mspot_results",
1228    glacier_only=False,
1229    target_mb=None,
1230):
1231    """
1232    Analyze the results of SPOTPY sampling for model calibration of the MATILDA model.
1233
1234    This function processes sampling results from SPOTPY to identify the best parameter set, evaluate performance,
1235    and optionally generate visualizations of the results.
1236
1237    Parameters
1238    ----------
1239    sampling_data : str or SPOTPY result object
1240        The file path to a SPOTPY results CSV file or a SPOTPY result object.
1241    obs : str or pandas.DataFrame
1242        The file path to observed data (in CSV format with 'Date' column) or a DataFrame containing observed data.
1243    algorithm : str
1244        The SPOTPY algorithm used for sampling (e.g., 'abc', 'dream', 'sceua').
1245    obj_dir : str, optional
1246        Direction of the objective function optimization, either 'maximize' or 'minimize'. Default is 'maximize'.
1247    fig_path : str, optional
1248        Path to save generated plots. If None, plots are not saved.
1249    dbname : str, optional
1250        Name for saving the database and plots. Default is 'mspot_results'.
1251    glacier_only : bool, optional
1252        If True, optimizes only for glacier-specific metrics (e.g., mass balance). Default is False.
1253    target_mb : float, optional
1254        Target mean annual mass balance for melt model calibration. If None, this metric is not considered. Default is None.
1255
1256    Returns
1257    -------
1258    dict
1259        A dictionary containing:
1260        - 'best_param': dict
1261            Best parameter set identified during sampling.
1262        - 'best_index': int
1263            Index of the best run in the SPOTPY results.
1264        - 'best_model_run': array
1265            Model output corresponding to the best parameter set.
1266        - 'best_objf': float
1267            Value of the objective function for the best parameter set.
1268        - 'best_simulation': pandas.Series (if glacier_only is False and target_mb is None)
1269            Simulated time series corresponding to the best parameter set.
1270        - 'sampling_plot': matplotlib.Figure (if applicable)
1271            Iteration vs. objective function plot.
1272        - 'best_run_plot': matplotlib.Figure (if applicable)
1273            Best simulation vs. observed data plot.
1274        - 'par_uncertain_plot': matplotlib.Figure (if applicable)
1275            Parameter uncertainty plot.
1276
1277    Notes
1278    -----
1279    - The objective function can be maximized (e.g., Kling-Gupta Efficiency) or minimized (e.g., Mean Absolute Error)
1280      based on the algorithm and obj_dir setting.
1281    - For glacier-specific calibration, only glacier mass balance data is considered.
1282
1283    References
1284    ----------
1285    - SPOTPY library:
1286      - Houska, T., Kraft, P., Chamorro-Chavez, A., & Breuer, L. (2015). "SPOTting Model Parameters Using a Ready-Made
1287        Python Package." PLOS ONE, 10(12), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0145180
1288      - GitHub repository: https://github.com/thouska/spotpy
1289    """
1290
1291    if isinstance(obs, str):
1292        if glacier_only:
1293            obs = pd.read_csv(obs)
1294        else:
1295            obs = pd.read_csv(obs, index_col="Date", parse_dates=["Date"])
1296
1297    if isinstance(sampling_data, str):
1298        if sampling_data.endswith(".csv"):
1299            sampling_data = sampling_data[: len(sampling_data) - 4]
1300        results = spotpy.analyser.load_csv_results(sampling_data)
1301    else:
1302        results = sampling_data.getdata()
1303
1304    maximize = ["abc", "dds", "demcz", "dream", "rope", "sa", "fscabc", "mcmc", "mle"]
1305    minimize = ["nsgaii", "padds", "sceua"]
1306    both = ["fast", "lhs", "mc"]
1307
1308    if algorithm in maximize:
1309        best_param = spotpy.analyser.get_best_parameterset(results)
1310    elif algorithm in minimize:
1311        best_param = spotpy.analyser.get_best_parameterset(results, maximize=False)
1312    elif algorithm in both:
1313        print(
1314            "WARNING: The selected algorithm "
1315            + algorithm
1316            + " can either maximize or minimize the objective function."
1317            " You can specify the direction by passing obj_dir to analyze_results(). The default is 'maximize'."
1318        )
1319        if obj_dir == "maximize":
1320            best_param = spotpy.analyser.get_best_parameterset(results)
1321        elif obj_dir == "minimize":
1322            best_param = spotpy.analyser.get_best_parameterset(results, maximize=False)
1323        else:
1324            raise ValueError(
1325                "Invalid argument for obj_dir. Choose 'minimize' or 'maximize'."
1326            )
1327    else:
1328        raise ValueError(
1329            "Invalid argument for algorithm. Available algorithms: ['abc', 'dds', 'demcz', 'dream', 'rope', 'sa',"
1330            "'fscabc', 'mcmc', 'mle', 'nsgaii', 'padds', 'sceua', 'fast', 'lhs', 'mc']"
1331        )
1332
1333    par_names = spotpy.analyser.get_parameternames(best_param)
1334    param_zip = zip(par_names, best_param[0])
1335    best_param = dict(param_zip)
1336
1337    if glacier_only:
1338        bestindex, bestobjf = spotpy.analyser.get_minlikeindex(
1339            results
1340        )  # Run with lowest MAE
1341        best_model_run = results[bestindex]
1342
1343    elif target_mb is not None:
1344        if obj_dir == "minimize":
1345            bestindex, bestobjf = spotpy.analyser.get_minlikeindex(results)
1346        else:
1347            bestindex, bestobjf = spotpy.analyser.get_maxlikeindex(results)
1348        best_model_run = results[bestindex]
1349
1350    else:
1351        sim_start = obs.index[0]
1352        sim_end = obs.index[-1]
1353        bestindex, bestobjf = spotpy.analyser.get_maxlikeindex(
1354            results
1355        )  # Run with highest KGE
1356        best_model_run = results[bestindex]
1357        fields = [word for word in best_model_run.dtype.names if word.startswith("sim")]
1358        best_simulation = pd.Series(
1359            list(list(best_model_run[fields])[0]),
1360            index=pd.date_range(sim_start, sim_end),
1361        )
1362        # Only necessary because obs has a datetime. Thus, both need a datetime.
1363
1364    if not glacier_only and target_mb is None:
1365        fig1 = plt.figure(1, figsize=(9, 5))
1366        plt.plot(results["like1"])
1367        plt.ylabel("KGE")
1368        plt.xlabel("Iteration")
1369        if fig_path is not None:
1370            plt.savefig(fig_path + "/" + dbname + "_sampling_plot.png")
1371
1372        fig2 = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 9))
1373        ax = plt.subplot(1, 1, 1)
1374        ax.plot(
1375            best_simulation,
1376            color="black",
1377            linestyle="solid",
1378            label="Best objf.=" + str(bestobjf),
1379        )
1380        ax.plot(obs, "r.", markersize=3, label="Observation data")
1381        plt.xlabel("Date")
1382        plt.ylabel("Discharge [mm d-1]")
1383        plt.legend(loc="upper right")
1384        if fig_path is not None:
1385            plt.savefig(fig_path + "/" + dbname + "_best_run_plot.png")
1386
1387        fig3 = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 9))
1388        ax = plt.subplot(1, 1, 1)
1389        q5, q95 = [], []
1390        for field in fields:
1391            q5.append(np.percentile(results[field][-100:-1], 2.5))
1392            q95.append(np.percentile(results[field][-100:-1], 97.5))
1393        ax.plot(q5, color="dimgrey", linestyle="solid")
1394        ax.plot(q95, color="dimgrey", linestyle="solid")
1395        ax.fill_between(
1396            np.arange(0, len(q5), 1),
1397            list(q5),
1398            list(q95),
1399            facecolor="dimgrey",
1400            zorder=0,
1401            linewidth=0,
1402            label="parameter uncertainty",
1403        )
1404        ax.plot(
1405            np.array(obs), "r.", label="data"
1406        )  # Need to remove Timestamp from Evaluation to make comparable
1407        # ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
1408        ax.set_xlim(0, len(obs))
1409        ax.legend()
1410        if fig_path is not None:
1411            plt.savefig(fig_path + "/" + dbname + "_par_uncertain_plot.png")
1412
1413        return {
1414            "best_param": best_param,
1415            "best_index": bestindex,
1416            "best_model_run": best_model_run,
1417            "best_objf": bestobjf,
1418            "best_simulation": best_simulation,
1419            "sampling_plot": fig1,
1420            "best_run_plot": fig2,
1421            "par_uncertain_plot": fig3,
1422        }
1423
1424    return {
1425        "best_param": best_param,
1426        "best_index": bestindex,
1427        "best_model_run": best_model_run,
1428        "best_objf": bestobjf,
1429    }
1430
